code.text: Sustained reduction in gait speed relative to this patient's own baseline

author.display: Digital Twin Engine deviation monitor (rolling robust z-score + CUSUM)

code.text: Statistical change detection against personal baseline

detail: Gait speed 0.94 m/s versus a 30-day personal rolling baseline of 1.12 m/s (SD 0.086), a deviation of -2.1 SD sustained across 4 consecutive days. CUSUM change point detected 2026-03-13. Detected 62 hours after change-point onset, within the 48-hour target measured from the point at which the deviation became statistically distinguishable. Baseline was established over 41 days of observation, exceeding the 14-day minimum required before any alert may fire.

action.text: Optional nurse-navigator outreach call. NOT an automated escalation — a human decides whether and how to act.

note.text: ALERT BUDGET: this alert was delivered. Current week volume 6 of an agreed ceiling of 11 per caseload. The ceiling was set in writing by the nurse-navigator team before launch and can only be changed through the same conversation. Deferred alerts are logged so that suppression is auditable.

METHOD NOTE: deviation detection deliberately uses statistics rather than machine learning. A rolling robust z-score with CUSUM is something the nurse-navigator can understand and challenge, which for this task is worth more than a marginally better black box. See ADR-0004.
